response: The clustering still lacks a coherent solar and stellar astrophysics cluster — papers on stellar abundances, stellar magnetic fields, solar active regions, chromospheric physics, stellar mixing, and stellar evolution are scattered across "Stellar Abundances and Observations," "Stellar Magnetic Fields Observations," "Plasma wave particle interactions," and "Astrophysical Gas and Spectroscopy" and should all be consolidated into one dedicated solar/stellar cluster. The "Multi-wavelength Astronomical Observations" cluster remains a catch-all mixing high-energy transients (pulsars, novae, quasars) with instrumentation topics and ISM papers — high-energy transient and compact object papers should join the high-energy cluster, ISM/molecular cloud papers should join galactic/extragalactic, and instrumentation/methods papers should form their own cluster. The "Simulation-Based Inference Methods" and "Astronomical Observation Interference Challenges" clusters are grouped by methodology rather than subject area and should be merged into a single instrumentation and methods cluster alongside other telescope, pipeline, and data-analysis papers.
